leave_apartment.text: Rain at the window. A kettle left on the counter. Somewhere above you, a door opens into the night.

meet_stranger.title: The stranger with the yellow umbrella
meet_stranger.text:
“You couldn’t sleep either?”
The stranger shifts a yellow umbrella to make room. A crooked paper star hangs from its handle.
“I’m taking this to someone who insists every umbrella needs a night sky. Platform 6, if you fancy a walk.”
The stranger nods to the cat. “Our smallest neighbour. Somehow always has the best seat.”

choices.label: Stand under the umbrella for a moment

read_board.title: WHERE DO YOU WANT TO GO
read_board.text:
The letters glow like a question someone has been saving for you.
A blank ticket waits on the bench. There is room for an answer later.
A neighbour steps around the cat. “Sorry, chief. Didn’t realise this was your platform.”

board_train.title: The conductor
board_train.text:
The conductor studies the blank ticket without trying to read it.
“No need to fill it in yet. You can keep the window seat. The latch sticks; lift it first.”
Inside, amber lamps warm the carriage. There is no hurry to answer anyone.

meet_passenger.title: Mira and the unopened camera
meet_passenger.text:
“I’m Mira. I mend wind-up boats. Mostly I explain to them that a circle is not a race.”
She taps a small unopened camera box against her knee, then catches herself and puts it down.
“I bought this for somewhere I haven’t been. I was expecting to know what to photograph by now. Would you like company at the next stop?”

choices.label: “Company is fine. I’m a bit quiet tonight.”

arrive_shore.title: A moonlit shore
arrive_shore.text:
The carriage door opens on salt air. A lighthouse, a stone arch and a scatter of stars wait beyond the low platform.
Mira tucks the camera under her arm.
“Oh. The water’s put the lighthouse upside down. Can we find where the two lights meet?”

return_train.title: Back in the carriage
return_train.text:
The conductor sets down two cups. One rattles on the table; Mira folds a spare timetable under the saucer.
“Precision marine engineering,” she says. “Usually costs more than a timetable.”
The conductor slides the toast within reach. “Orange marmalade, or the mysterious jar? It’s plum. I ought to label it.”

have_breakfast.title: Breakfast at night
have_breakfast.text:
Toast, plum jam and wheels finding their rhythm. Mira opens the window a crack; the sea stays with you a little longer.
A postcard rests by the jam: THE UNFINISHED FAIR. Its tiny painted boats lean stubbornly sideways.
“My next delivery,” Mira says. “One repaired boat. Three still sulking. I wonder if the fair has opened yet.”

choices.label: Let the train carry you on

finish.title: A journey to keep
finish.text:
You keep a small ticket stamped PLATFORM 6.
There is no right way to have spent the night.
Outside, another station is beginning to glow.

ending.title: STILL HERE
ending.text:
Chapter one complete
Souvenir: a ticket from Platform 6
Thank you for being here.

camera.title: “I thought it would feel bigger.”
camera.text:
“I thought it would feel bigger,” Mira says.
She means the moment, then laughs at how difficult that is to explain. A wave folds quietly through the arch.
The little camera waits between you. You can decide what to do with it.

optional.title: A small invitation · entirely optional
optional.text:
If you feel like it, notice one ordinary thing near you for a moment: a cup, a window, the room around you.
Nothing to prove or record. The journey continues either way.

pet_cat.title: A small purr
pet_cat.text: The cat leans into your hand. Apparently, you have passed the sniff inspection.

umbrella_question.title: A paper sky
umbrella_question.text:
“Tonight? The coast,” the stranger says. “After that, I consult the board. I’m excellent at reading departure times and terrible at packing sandwiches.”
They straighten the paper star. “This is for my sister. She’s covering the late shift.”

umbrella_quiet.title: Under the umbrella
umbrella_quiet.text:
Rain ticks on the yellow canopy. The stranger hums two notes, loses the tune, and lets it go.
After a while they tilt the umbrella toward the stair door. “Ready when you are.”

passenger_boats.title: Boats with opinions
passenger_boats.text:
“Little clockwork ones. My aunt built a pond at her traveling fair. Every boat turns left. I’ve checked the gears, the rudders, even the pond.”
Mira smiles. “I’m beginning to suspect the ducks.”
She makes room by the window. “We can investigate a much bigger body of water first.”

passenger_quiet.title: Room for quiet
passenger_quiet.text:
“That works. I sometimes need a while before the words catch up.”
Mira moves her tool roll from the empty seat. Inside are miniature screwdrivers and a bent brass propeller.
“I might point at things. You don’t have to produce a speech.”

shore_lighthouse.title: Two lights
shore_lighthouse.text:
A tall line of amber reaches down into the sea. Mira crouches beside you, far back from the water.
“There. When the wave flattens, the lamp and its reflection almost touch. Like someone joining two halves of a drawing.”
From the viewing marker, the lighthouse is the tall shape on the left.

shore_lighthouse_joke.title: A candle for the coast
shore_lighthouse_joke.text:
“We’d need a magnificent cake,” Mira says. “And a less windy birthday.”
The next small wave separates the two lights again.

shore_arch.title: A doorway for waves
shore_arch.text:
A small wave threads the stone arch, then fans into a silver line.
Mira traces its path with one finger. “The doorway stays still. Everything passing through it changes shape.”
From the viewing marker, the arch is the middle shape; the lighthouse is to its left.

choices.label: Follow the next wave with your eyes

shore_arch_joke.title: No timetable
shore_arch_joke.text: “And it never apologizes for the delay.” Mira turns her unopened camera box over. “I could learn that part. The boats could not.”

shore_constellation.title: The crooked trail
shore_constellation.text:
Five stars climb above the water. Mira holds up the bent brass propeller from her tool roll, matching its crooked angle to the trail.
“Not a useful measurement. But it’s a good shape.”
The rising stars are the shape on the right. Together with the lighthouse and arch, they make one picture.

choices.label: Trace the shape in the air

shore_stars_reply.title: A spare shape
shore_stars_reply.text:
“I was going to straighten it. Maybe I’ll make it a sign for the boat stall instead.”
Mira slips it back into the tool roll, leaving the decision for another day.

train_window.title: The window seat
train_window.text:
You lift the latch before sliding it. Rain beads run sideways over the outside glass; a lit signal passes, then another.
A paper timetable has been folded into a little boat on the windowsill. Someone has written NOT SEAWORTHY beneath it.

choices.label: Leave the paper boat for the next passenger

breakfast_postcard.title: The Unfinished Fair
breakfast_postcard.text:
On the back, a hand-drawn arrow points to a pond. OPEN WHEN THE KETTLE BOILS, someone has written.
Mira adds, “My aunt’s opening hours are unusually specific and completely unreliable.”
The conductor checks the dark window. “We’ll find out when we arrive.”
For now, there is still warm toast.

choices.label: Let the train carry you on

objectives.apartment: The roof door is open. Go upstairs when you’re ready.
objectives.roof: Meet the stranger beneath the yellow umbrella.
objectives.platform: Read the station board and take the blank ticket.
objectives.conductor: Show the conductor your ticket and board Platform 6.
objectives.passenger: Meet Mira by the window. There’s room for quiet company.
objectives.shoreline: The train has stopped by the sea. Walk to the carriage door.
objectives.overlook: Explore the three shore shapes, then frame them at the viewing marker
objectives.camera_choice: Mira’s camera is waiting. Choose how to keep this moment.
objectives.optional_action: A small invitation is optional. Both answers continue the night.
objectives.return_train: The warm carriage is waiting. Join Mira at the breakfast table.
objectives.breakfast: Share breakfast. The fair postcard has a next-stop hint.
objectives.complete: Keep the Platform 6 ticket, then choose whether to continue to the fair.

arrive_shore.text: Mira points toward the reflected lighthouse, then leaves a quiet space beside you.
“A much bigger pond,” Mira says. “And fewer suspicious ducks.”

camera.text: The crooked brass propeller stays tucked in her tool roll, waiting for its possible life as a sign.

return_train.text: Mira slides a cup into the empty place without filling the quiet with a question.
“If only all the boats needed was a folded timetable,” Mira says.

finish.text: The postcard’s arrow points toward the pond at the Unfinished Fair. Mira has one repaired boat ready to deliver.
